title: Ethics & CSR
examples: What is the difference between profit and ethics in business?
Can a business make money and still be ethical?
When do businesses have to consider society?

explain.say: Today we are learning about business ethics and social responsibility.

items: Business ethics is about right and wrong.

explain.say: An ethical decision considers what is right for everyone involved.
A concrete example is deciding on product safety for children.
Another example is how a company treats its workers fairly.
A third example is deciding on packaging waste for the planet.
In real life, think about buying a phone made with conflict minerals.

faq.q: What is the difference between ethics and law?
faq.a: Laws are rules set by government and are mandatory. Ethics are moral principles about right and wrong that a business chooses to follow.
asks: Is ethics the same as law?
Do businesses have to follow ethics?

faq.q: Does CSR mean spending money on charity?
faq.a: CSR is broader than just donating money. It means operating in a way that benefits society and the environment.
asks: Is charity the only form of CSR?

faq.q: What is a trade-off in business?
faq.a: A trade-off means giving up one benefit to gain another. Businesses often have to balance these competing needs.
asks: When do businesses have to choose between two things?

faq.q: Can a business be profitable and ethical at the same time?
faq.a: Yes, many argue that long-term profit relies on ethical practices and good community relations.
asks: Is profit and ethics mutually exclusive?

faq.a: Stakeholders are anyone affected by the business, like workers, customers, and the community. Ethics requires considering all of them.
asks: Who does a business need to worry about?
What are the different groups affected by a company?

facts: Ethical decisions involve balancing profit with moral considerations.
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) involves a business giving back to society.
A trade-off is a necessary compromise between two desirable but conflicting goals.
Stakeholders include employees, customers, owners, and the community.

quiz.say: A company decides to use only locally sourced materials even if they cost more.

options.show: The law does not require this level of sourcing.
options.say: The law does not require this level of sourcing.

options.show: This shows a commitment to ethical sourcing.
options.say: This shows a commitment to ethical sourcing.

options.show: This is purely a marketing tactic.
options.say: This is purely a marketing tactic.

options.show: This will definitely lower our profit margin.
options.say: This will definitely lower our profit margin.

quiz.why: Choosing local materials supports the community, which is an ethical consideration.

wrong.0: The law sets minimums; ethics requires going above the minimum standard.
wrong.2: While it can be marketed, the decision itself reflects a genuine ethical concern.
wrong.3: While costs increase, ethical practices can build brand loyalty and long-term value.

quiz.say: A business must choose between hiring more workers or increasing shareholder dividends.

options.show: The workers can negotiate a better deal later.
options.say: The workers can negotiate a better deal later.

options.show: The business must weigh the impact on people versus owners.
options.say: The business must weigh the impact on people versus owners.

options.show: It should always prioritize shareholder dividends.
options.say: It should always prioritize shareholder dividends.

options.show: The law dictates the correct balance.
options.say: The law dictates the correct balance.

quiz.why: This is a classic trade-off between stakeholder needs: employees and shareholders.

wrong.0: Ethical planning requires addressing the needs proactively, not waiting for conflict.
wrong.2: Ignoring workers' needs can damage the company's reputation and stability.
wrong.3: Laws set minimums, but ethics requires considering the best outcome for all parties.

quiz.say: When deciding on packaging, a business chooses biodegradable plastic over cheaper, non-recyclable plastic.

options.show: The customer will not notice the difference.
options.say: The customer will not notice the difference.

options.show: It will only affect the manufacturing cost.
options.say: It will only affect the manufacturing cost.

options.show: We can use non-recyclable plastic if we educate people.
options.say: We can use non-recyclable plastic if we educate people.

options.show: This prioritizes environmental impact over immediate cost savings.
options.say: This prioritizes environmental impact over immediate cost savings.

quiz.why: Biodegradability shows consideration for the environment, a key part of CSR.

wrong.0: Modern consumers are increasingly aware of and judge businesses by their environmental impact.
wrong.1: It also affects the consumer's perception and the planet's long-term health.
wrong.2: Education alone often fails against the sheer volume of waste produced.
